Hi Samir —

Thanks for the questions. High-level benchmark summary below (shortened for email). I’ve attached the full Q1 bench PDF with configs and raw numbers (redwood_benchmarks_Q1_2026.pdf). Happy to run a few spot checks against a short sample of your prompts if that would be useful.

Test config notes (see PDF for full table):
- Sequence length for main runs: 512 tokens (prefix + generation).
- Batch size = 1 (interactive latency), and micro-batching/batched throughput numbers also included.
- Quantization: q4_K / q4_0 variants we recommend for 70B/13B respectively to balance quality and runtime memory.

Key numbers (end-to-end, model token generation latency / throughput):
- 13B (q4_0) on A100 80GB:
  - p50 token latency: ~6–9 ms/token
  - p95 token latency: ~12–18 ms/token
  - 1-request, 256-token completion (end-to-end including decoding): ~1.8–2.5s
  - sustained throughput (concurrent streaming tokens): ~180–220 tokens/sec

- 70B (q4_K) on A100 80GB:
  - p50 token latency: ~18–30 ms/token
  - p95 token latency: ~35–55 ms/token
  - 1-request, 256-token completion: ~4.6–7.7s
  - sustained throughput: ~45–80 tokens/sec

- 70B (q4_K) on T4 (cost-optimized single-GPU): expect ~2–3x slower per-token latencies vs A100 and lower peak throughput (useful for PoC but not target production if you need tight latency).

Batching notes and KV cache behaviour:
- Small-batch interactive traffic (batch size 1–4) gives best latency/cost tradeoff for agent sessions. Larger batching improves GPU utilization and lowers per-token cost but adds queuing latency.
- Redwood’s KV cache + prefix caching can reduce end-to-end work for repeated context (agent prompt templates + customer history). For typical agent templates with 2–3 token prefixes repeated, we’ve seen token compute reduce by ~12–25% depending on cache hit rates.

Operational recommendations for your SLOs:
- If your hard target is ~200ms p50 for full completions (not per-token), 70B will be challenging for sub-second completions unless you allow more aggressive batching or accept higher latency for tail. 13B quantized deployments on A100 are a pragmatic starting point for sub-second interactive experiences for shorter completions (<=128 tokens).
- For the pilot we usually recommend: run 13B quant (q4_0) on A100 or T4 for cost-controlled PoC, measure with your prompt set, then scale to a 70B quant variant if you need higher generation quality and can accept higher latency or use multi-GPU sharding for throughput.

Attachments: redwood_benchmarks_Q1_2026.pdf (bench details + configs)

If helpful, we can provision a short, free eval run on a dedicated instance with your sample prompts (1–2 days) — I can coordinate the infra. Let me know what timeline works and I’ll route the request.

Cheers,
Aditya Rao
Applied ML / Inference Performance
Redwood Inference
